title: Content novelty artifact v1
description: What one context artifact adds to one model: knowledge atoms extracted from its text, the paired added/redundant/degraded/still_missing outcome per atom under two grading strictnesses, span-level attribution, content categories, and shortening candidates scored on five separate axes. Not comparable across models: novelty is a property of the (artifact, model) pair.

run_config.description: Seed, probe arms and budgets, stage switches, which files of the artifact were read, and a digest of the stage prompts. Two cells compare only when this block matches. `tier` is the named cost tier the run was launched at, if any, and carries `forfeits`: the claims a run at that tier may not make. The cost is probe-budget bound (~4 model calls per paired probe, measured), so a cheap tier buys its saving by giving up probe kinds and atoms, not by skipping cheap stages -- the forfeits say which.

ref_digest.description: Digest of exactly the files this cell measured (bundle.measured_digest: each measured file's path and text digest, in order), so a stored result cannot drift from the artifact it describes and an entry-point run never shares a digest with a bundle run. Not the subject scorecard's subject.ref_digest, which hashes every file under the subject path to identify the subject tree.

model.description: The model under measurement — the 'who did not already know this' half of the pair.

judge_model.description: Grading model. Equal to `model` only when the run passed --allow-self-judge, which is recorded as a warning.

sampling.description: How the probed subset was chosen (e.g. cap-per-artifact:120). Present so a capped run is never read as a full sweep.

faithfulness.description: Tally of supported/distorted/unsupported atoms against their own spans. Bounds distortion only; extractor recall is unmeasured.

paired.description: The 2x2 under each grading strictness. Both are required: the 6-way judge scale had only 0.664 inter-rater agreement, so no single collapse is authoritative.

k0.description: The model's prior recall over the artifact's own knowledge, with no artifact in context.

items.description: Item analysis over the probes -- which of them measure anything. kind_agreement asks, inside one run, whether an atom's own question and its rewording got the same verdict in the same arm (reversal probes excluded: their key is refusal, so disagreeing is their job); disagreement means that atom's outcome is wording-dependent, which is exactly what a `redundant` verdict must not be. discrimination is the classical point-biserial across models, with the models as respondents, and is only computable from three or more cells over the same atom set -- a single run reports measured:false with the reason rather than a number. Neither check judges whether an atom is true: an atom every model knows separates nothing and is still correct, while a negative r (the weaker models passed it more often) is the one to read as a defect.

bundle.description: Which files of the artifact were measured. A skill is a bundle: measured over the 33-skill study corpus 0.72 of all words live outside SKILL.md (per skill median 0.43, worst 0.99), so an entry-point-only run (include_resources false) is not comparable with a bundle run and must not be quoted as describing the artifact. outside_share is the on-disk share outside the entry point whether or not it was read; measurable_outside_share nets out policy_excluded_words (role decisions such as the skill's own evals, the same in both modes) and is the figure the warnings and report quote, since a rerun with --include-resources cannot read those; measured_share is the share of the readable words this run read (null when a file did not decode or there are no readable words); unmeasured_words is what such a rerun would add; excluded lists every file left out with its reason and a kind (symlink, not_text, unreadable, policy, budget, not_requested), and every reader interprets a row by the kind's class (novelty.bundle.EXCLUSION_CLASS): budget and not_requested are a gap (counted in unmeasured_words and warned about), policy is a decision (never charged as unread, and outside the readable-words denominator the warnings, the report and, for a record stamped coverage_basis readable, the gate uses), unreadable is unknown (the gate reports no artifact_coverage value while one exists; the warnings, note and report still quote a figure that leaves its words out), symlink and not_text are not content; pointer_spans names the spans whose only content is a path into the bundle, which carry no knowledge by design and are therefore not waste; by_source cuts the paired outcomes by the file that carried each atom. A bundle run measures what the artifact COULD deliver if the agent read all of it -- an upper bound; whether the agent loads a file at runtime is the agentic track's question.

coverage_basis.description: What the gate's artifact_coverage share is a share of. readable: the entry point plus the bundled words some run could read (policy_excluded_words left out), the basis of measurable_outside_share and of the analyzer's warnings, so the gate judges the figure the warnings quote. all_bundled_words: the entry point plus every bundled word on disk, role decisions included. Every record is now written with readable; a record without this field was written before it existed and is read as all_bundled_words, so its gate value does not change when it is re-gated.

measured_digest.description: Equal to artifact.ref_digest; carried in the record so atoms.json and probes.json name the text they were extracted from or probed against.

by_source.description: Per-file atom counts and paired outcomes. An atom is attributed to the file of its first cited span. A file with spans no extraction call read carries n_spans_unread and tokens_unread; a file none of whose spans was read has n_atoms null and unread true, rather than reading as a file that yields no knowledge.

probes.description: Probe budget and the fidelity of generated wordings. Paraphrase and reversal wordings come from a model and are checked mechanically (anchor tokens preserved, polarity actually flipped, answer not leaked into the question) before they are asked; rejects are dropped, never probed. malformed_rate is the share rejected: it bounds how much of the claimed probe budget a kind actually got, and a non-trivial rate means the kind covers fewer atoms than `atoms.n`. Empty when no wording generator ran (direct probes only).

reasons.description: Rejection reason tally. Mechanical reasons only; a clean result is the absence of detectable corruption, not proof of fidelity.

by_knowledge_kind.description: The same paired 2x2, cut by what each atom IS: its kind, and each of its tags. Keyed by scoring. Tag slices overlap (an atom carries several tags) and must never be summed. Slices below min_probes carry n_paired and underpowered:true and no rates. Both labels are one extractor's opinion: three extractors agreed on which spans carry knowledge (Jaccard 0.87-0.99) and disagreed by up to 2.5x on the labels, `local` and `public` worst, so a per-tag rate must name its extractor and a per-tag gate needs a reproducible tag vocabulary first.

arms.description: Mean correctness per arm per scoring. `placebo` (domain-mismatched text of similar length) and `shuffled` (same spans, order destroyed) are controls, not treatments.

reversal_resisted.description: Fraction of planted-inversion probes refused. Lower is worse, and it got worse with model strength in the study.

abstentions.description: Per-arm abstention counts; a deferral-phrasing defect shows up here before it shows up in a score.

confidence_correlation.description: Correlation between stated confidence and graded correctness. Recorded as a warning signal; never used as a score.

order_independent.description: True when the shuffled control scored at least as high as the artifact as written.

categories.description: Atom counts per content category. The known/new axis is measured; the useful/inert axis is judged and had 71.6% reviewer agreement.

conflicts.description: Atom pairs that cannot both be true. Says 'these disagree', not 'this one is wrong' — deciding that needs a primary source.

conflict_coverage.description: How much of the atom-pair space the conflict check compared. pairs_compared counts pairs that shared an answered call; pairs_total is every pair among the extracted atoms, which is the capped sample when spans.capped_atom_set is true. pairs_compared <= pairs_total is not expressible here and is enforced by the gate. A run that left pairs_compared below pairs_total, or capped the atom set, does not clear harmful_atoms at a count of 0.

frac_carrying_nothing.description: Upper bound on dead weight, not a measurement of it. Over the text extraction read: spans no extraction call could read (n_unread) are outside both the numerator and the denominator. Read it only together with capped_atom_set: derived from a capped atom set it does not approximate the full-set figure but inverts it (0.064 became 0.743 on the study's largest artifact). Extractor recall is not the limit here: three extractors cited the same spans, Jaccard 0.87-0.99.

n_unread.description: Spans no extraction call could read, even one span per call, and that carry no atom. What they assert is unknown, so they are not counted as carrying nothing; extraction.unread_span_ids names them.

n_atoms_indexed.description: How many atoms were indexed onto the spans to compute the dead-token share. Its ratio to the artifact's full atom count is what makes the figure readable.

capped_atom_set.description: True when the indexed atom set hit the extraction cap. The dead-token share is then a property of the sample, not of the artifact, and must not be quoted as the latter.

extraction.description: What atom extraction could not read, and what re-asking cost. An unparseable batch, or one with no usable atom, is split in half and re-asked down to one span per call; a failed call or an empty reply is not (an empty reply is what a reasoning model returns when it spends the output ceiling, so the warning names it with the --max-tokens fix). Absent from artifacts written before it existed.

unread_span_ids.description: Spans no extraction call could read, in document order. Labelled `unread` in the span views, left out of frac_carrying_nothing and dead weight, and kept by every shortening candidate.

unparseable_span_ids.description: The unread spans whose reply arrived but did not parse even alone: an output ceiling too low for one span (raise --max-tokens). The rest were lost to a failed call or an empty reply.

unusable_span_ids.description: The unread spans whose reply parsed and had rows, none of them an atom (wrong keys, strings, span ids that are not the document's). An empty array is a result and is not listed.

retried_batches.description: Batches whose reply did not parse, or had no usable atom, and were split and re-asked.

calls.description: Extraction calls made, splits included. An n-span batch that never parses costs up to 2n-1 calls.

batches.description: Calls the same extraction would make with no splitting: batches the run reached (a capped run stops early), each counted once whatever its halves cost.

last_error.description: The last error on a span that stayed unread; errors a split recovered from are not recorded.

reached.description: How far through the input a capped atom set reached; null when the cap did not bind. The input is the text that was segmented into spans: the entry point, plus on a bundle run the files its roles and budgets selected; bundled files it left out are in no span, so none of these figures counts them (bundle.measured_share says how much of the artifact went into the input). Extraction walks the spans in document order and stops at the cap, so a capped set covers the input up to the span it stopped at, not a sample of it. last_span is the last span any kept atom cites among the spans some call was sent (not the last batch sent: a batch the cap cut mid-reply was sent whole; nor a cited span no call was sent), spans the count of the input's spans up to and including it, of all the input's spans, and tokens_share those spans' share of the input's span tokens. Absent from artifacts written before it existed.

carrier_confirmation.description: Result of checking each atom against the span the extractor cited for it. Absent when the run skipped the check (--no-confirm-carriers), in which case the labels report the citation as given and must not be presented as confirmed. Measured on 257 atoms: 0.833 of atoms recovered from the bare cited span, 0.907 with the span's heading path prepended (~16 tokens), and 0.19 not recoverable from the cited file at all.

unlocated_atoms.description: Atom ids the oracle could not recover from any cited span, truncated. Not defects by default: the faithfulness check called 46 of 49 such atoms supported, so they read as syntheses of the whole document and render as unlocated rather than colouring a span.

needs.description: Need-graph statistics. The graph is built from the artifact's name and description only, so the artifact cannot define its own relevance.

out_of_scope_atoms.description: Atoms whose best need match is an out-of-scope node: text answering a question this artifact's task does not pose.

retention.description: What the retention oracle did. escalation_rate is the cost knob; adjudicator null means the run was lexical-only and cannot see contradictions.

llm_errors.description: Escalations with no usable adjudicator verdict: the call failed, the reply did not parse, or it parsed and named no verdict. Each is answered absent for that decision and is not cached, on disk or in the response cache.

shortening.description: Candidate packages, each scored on five axes that are never collapsed into one retention number.

value_coverage.description: Share of atoms whose `value` weight came from a measured relevance and outcome rather than the 0.5 fallback. Low coverage means `value` is atom coverage per token under a value label; in the study per-model value was defined for 148 of 2422 atoms, because it needs a measured per-model K0.

value_is_coverage_proxy.description: True when value_coverage < 0.5. Do not rank candidates by `value` when this is set.

protection.description: Share of protected spans kept. A candidate below 1.0 is a different artifact, not a smaller one.

topics.description: Spans rolled up by their first two headings, largest first: spans, tokens, label counts, added_spans, dead_tokens (tokens of `empty` spans) and unread_tokens (tokens of `unread` spans, which no extraction call read and which are not dead weight).

replayed_calls.description: Calls served from the response cache; left out of the token and usd totals.

usd.description: null when any call this run paid for had unknown pricing, a call returned no usage, or no call was made — distinct from a genuinely free run. Replayed calls are left out of the sum.

caveats.description: Travels with the numbers on purpose, so a quoted rate carries its limits.

knowledge_slices.description: Slice name -> paired outcome rates for the atoms in that slice.

underpowered.description: Set instead of rates when the slice has fewer than min_probes paired probes. A rate on a 2-probe slice is noise with a decimal point.
